Measurements are in a plane perpendicular to the pedicle axis through the isthmus. The table prints ± without defining its statistic. Cohort: 57 patients, 49 female and 8 male; Lenke 1 (25) or Lenke 2 (32), 684 pedicles. Enrolled ages 12–20, Table 1 age 16.2 ± 2.4; 10–20 is the abstract inclusion range. The paper states right is always convex and left always concave. Per-cell observation counts are not supplied.

definitions.section: Figure 1 caption; Table 1; places of the measurement-count and population statements not recorded
definitions.text: Figure 1 defines transverse diameter as “the medial-lateral inner and outer cortical width of the pedicle” measured at the isthmus. Three measurements per parameter at the isthmus were averaged. Table 1 does not label which of its two rows is inner or outer: assigning the first row as inner and second as outer is this project’s own inference. The paper does not define the ± statistic; interpreting it as SD is this project’s own inference. The paper states a total of 120 children aged 5–14, selected by stratified random sampling; per-age-band and sex counts are not stated.

APEX±1, the region of the AV and its two adjacent vertebrae; H, cortical pedicle height; h, cancellous pedicle height; NV ± 1, the region of the NV and its two adjacent vertebrae; W, cortical pedicle width; w, cancellous pedicle width

definitions.section: Fig. 1 caption, Table 2 footnotes and Discussion; places of the quoted measurement sentence and the side statement not recorded
definitions.text: Measured by "cutting out pedicles in a plane perpendicular to the pedicle axis through the isthmus". Fig. 1 names W cortical pedicle width and w cancellous pedicle width; the discussion treats W as the outer diameter. Right pedicle is always convex; left pedicle is always concave. H is cortical pedicle height and h cancellous pedicle height. Per-cell n is not supplied.
